steps.title: Volume: how much was traded
steps.text:
**Volume** is how much was traded in each period. It's shown as the bars along the bottom of the chart.

High volume means lots of participation. Low volume means few traders were active.

steps.title: Volume confirms moves
steps.text:
Look at the chart again: while price moved sideways, volume was **quiet**. When price broke higher, volume **jumped**.

A breakout on high volume shows many traders are behind the move. A move on very low volume is easier to reverse.

steps.question: Price breaks above a level on the highest volume of the month. What does that suggest?
options: The move is guaranteed to continue
Volume has nothing to do with price
steps.explanation: High volume shows **conviction**: many traders acted. It makes the move more believable, but nothing in trading is guaranteed.

steps.title: Liquidity
steps.text:
**Liquidity** is how easily you can trade **without moving the price**.

**Liquid** markets (large company shares, EUR/USD, Bitcoin) have many buyers and sellers, tight spreads and smooth prices.

**Illiquid** markets have wide spreads and prices that jump around.

steps.title: A note on forex volume
steps.text:
Forex has no single central exchange, so forex charts usually show **tick volume**: the number of price changes reported by your data provider, not the true amount traded.

It's still a useful rough measure of activity.

steps.question: Which is usually a sign of an illiquid market?
options: Wide spreads and sudden price jumps
steps.explanation: Few participants means big gaps between bids and asks, so even small orders can move the price.

points: **Volume** shows how much was traded in each period.
Moves on **high volume** carry more conviction.
**Liquidity** means you can trade easily without moving the price.
